issue.title: Neomake and Deoplete combination causes Segmentation fault on save and exit

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
- Neovim version: Master (0.1.5-69-g81e0874) **Not present in 0.1.4**
- Operating system/version: Gentoo Linux (Hardened Musl x86_64)
- Terminal name/version: st 0.6
- `$TERM`: st-256color
### Actual behaviour

Segmentation fault on closing and saving file (:x :wq)
### Expected behaviour

No segfault!
### Steps to reproduce:

The segmentation fault appears to be triggered when I do the following:
1. Have neomake and deoplete enabled (note: i am using vim-plug)
vimrc:

``` viml
call plug#begin('~/.config/nvim/plugged')
Plug 'benekastah/neomake'
Plug 'Shougo/deoplete.vim'
call plug#end()

let g:deoplete#enable_at_startup=1
autocmd! BufWritePost * Neomake
```
1. Insert a line in a  **tex** file.
2. save and exit

body:
Can you get a non-optimized backtrace? Is the repo step really just a single `call` command?

Just curious, does "hardened musl" make an effort to expose segfaults?

Yes. It appears to be simpler than that.

No, not that I know of. I know that musl attempts to be more compliant with the C standard than GLIBC, and that does include some slightly different behavior in stdio. The hardened bit comes from using a PAX kernel and setting -fPIE on all builds.

Now I built neovim in debug mode and ran it from the build directory with no init.vim in ~/.config/nvim, and it still segfaults.

```
./nvim -u NONE
```

`msg_puts_printf` calls `mch_errmsg` which is `#define`d to `fprintf`, which apparently on your system is replaced by `fputs`.

```
fputs (s=0x3cd9b967b40 "E", f=0x3b07dfa9b00 <__stderr_used>)
```

This is the first iteration of the loop in `msg_puts_printf`. And `msg_puts_printf` has not changed for 2 years.

I can't see what could possibly be causing this. Would you be able to run with ASAN enabled? https://github.com/neovim/neovim/wiki/Development-tips#debugging-program-errors-undefined-behavior-leaks-

found https://github.com/facebook/folly/issues/310 and http://comments.gmane.org/gmane.linux.lib.musl.general/2189
Can you confirm that Vim (please say what `:version`) compiled with the same environment/compiler/stdlib, does not have this issue? (Make sure to cause it to write to stderr on startup.)

Unfortunately, UBSAN/ASAN etc. don't work on musl at the moment.. I think they might be fixed in GCC 6.1.0?

I know that one of the optimizations that GCC does is to convert calls to fprintf to fputs when there are no positional arguments other than the format string and the FILE*

The only thing I think could be likely is that musl's default thread stack size is 80k (as opposed to GLIBC's default thread stack of ~5MB), which you can hit really easily if you're not careful, and does cause segmentation faults (but I haven't checked neovim's code to see whether that is true). http://wiki.musl-libc.org/wiki/Functional_differences_from_glibc
